family.tagline: A rented walk-up flat, an easel and one Companion Core.
family.story: Lindiwe plans a housing charity’s campaigns from the study alcove. Matthias writes features at the dining table, and Tamsin paints at her easel. The Core sits on a writing desk in the living room.

home.lede: A three-storey walk-up of warm yellow brick, with white sash windows and a stone stoop up to the street door. The family’s flat fills the first floor up, with an iron balcony. A walled brick court lies behind the block.

spots.line: A writing desk, a task chair and a bookshelf in a nook off the passage.
A chesterfield sofa, a patterned rug and the Core on its writing desk.
A glass table, two Windsor chairs and a chandelier.
A range, a fridge and a run of counters along one wall.
A loft bed, a small desk and an easel by the wall.

day.line: Monday starts with three jobs and a timer.
Matthias moves a pitch card along the fridge.
Lunch at the counter settles the week’s dinners.
Matthias saves a council page before it changes.
Rooibos fills the tracker while Lindiwe reads along.
Tamsin finishes a painting, and Lindiwe takes its picture.
Tamsin curls up on the sofa with her story.
Sunday’s long reads wait out in the back court.

members.name: Lindiwe
members.work: marketing lead at a housing charity

companion.name: Rooibos
companion.job: Opens Grist in its own browser and fills the rows Lindiwe reads out.
companion.limits: Fills rows only. Lindiwe reads every row before it stands.

profile.bio: Lindiwe plans a housing charity’s campaigns from the study alcove. Her lists, drawings and trackers sit on the Core, and Rooibos fills in the rows she reads out.

companion.name: Caraway
companion.job: Drafts chase notes from the lines Matthias texts it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Matthias reads and sends every note.

profile.bio: Matthias writes features at the dining table. His saved pages, tapes and drafts sit on the Core, and Caraway drafts the chase notes that he reads before they go.
Tamsin paints at her easel and listens to stories on the sofa. Her paintings and drawings sit on the Core, where the family can find them again.

popup.title: A parcel waits up the stoop
popup.body: Matthias carries the parcel up the stoop and the stairs to the living room. Tamsin counts the steps out loud, all the way up.

popup.title: Matthias lifts out the Companion Core
popup.body: Matthias sets the Companion Core on the writing desk. Tamsin lays the power cable, the quick-start guide and the recovery USB drive out on the rug.

popup.title: Plug in, then press the button
popup.body: Lindiwe plugs the Core in, and Tamsin presses the button. It wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Joining the Core from Lindiwe’s phone
popup.body: Lindiwe joins the Core’s own network from her phone’s Wi-Fi settings. Then she picks the flat’s home network.

popup.title: Two agents, then two apps
popup.body: Lindiwe browses the Companion Hub store from the writing desk and picks OpenClaw and Hermes. The family adds HomeHub and Linkwarden, then walks away.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Lindiwe names her agent Rooibos
popup.body: Lindiwe names her agent Rooibos and sends a first message. A reply comes back, the Core beside her.

say.speaker: lindiwe
say.text: Hello, Lindiwe. Rooibos here. What first?

detail.before: Lindiwe kept the charity’s campaign chores in her head and typed each one into a tracker herself.
detail.after: Rooibos runs in its own sandbox on the Core. Lindiwe names a chore, and Rooibos prepares it for her to approve.
steps: Pick OpenClaw in the Companion Hub store
Give the agent a name
Say hello and name the first chore
detail.fact: OpenClaw is an agent with its own browser, running in its own sandbox on your Core.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: Banner ads fade on every device
popup.body: The router now asks Pi-hole on the Core for every name lookup. Tamsin’s tablet, both phones and the laptop meet fewer banner ads.

detail.before: Name lookups went to NextDNS, set up one device at a time, so the tablet was often missed.
detail.after: Pi-hole answers every name lookup on the Core, and the router sends all the flat’s devices through it.
steps: Point the router at Pi-hole
Open a page on the tablet
Add a wrongly blocked site to the allow list
detail.fact: Pi-hole blocks ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level.

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off

popup.title: Tamsin’s story waits where she stopped
popup.body: Tamsin curls up on the sofa with a story from the family’s own files. Audiobookshelf on the Core remembers where she stopped, so tomorrow starts there.

detail.before: Tamsin’s stories played in the Audible app, and her place in each one was kept there.
detail.after: Audiobookshelf holds the story files the family already has on the Core and remembers where each listener stopped.
steps: Add the story files to the library
Press play on the tablet
Come back to the same place
detail.fact: Audiobookshelf lets you listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off on any device.

beats.capability: send a note or file as a one-time link that destroys itself after it is read

popup.title: A password that is read once
popup.body: The landlord’s repairs site sends one temporary password, and Matthias passes it to Lindiwe. The Cryptgeon note on the Core disappears once she has read it.

detail.before: A temporary password used to travel in a text thread or a Privnote link.
detail.after: Cryptgeon on the Core makes a one-time note. Once Lindiwe opens it, the note is gone.
steps: Write the password into a new note
Send Lindiwe the one-time link
Open it once on the home Wi-Fi
detail.fact: Cryptgeon sends a note or file as a one-time link that destroys itself after it is read.

beats.capability: a link page for your business or yourself, like Linktree

popup.title: The poster’s page, tested at home
popup.body: The winter campaign poster needs one page that lists its links. Lindiwe builds it in LinkStack on the Core and tests it on her phone over the flat’s Wi-Fi.
popup.note: Only devices on the home Wi-Fi reach this page.

detail.before: The poster’s links lived on a Linktree page that had to be edited online.
detail.after: LinkStack builds the same page on the Core. Lindiwe tests each link from her phone on the home Wi-Fi.
steps: Add the poster’s links one by one
Open the page on a phone
Fix any link that does not open
detail.fact: LinkStack is a link page for your business or yourself, like Linktree.

beats.capability: save web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot

popup.title: The council reworded its minutes
popup.body: A council page was reworded overnight, but Matthias had saved it earlier. Linkwarden on the Core kept a screenshot and a PDF of the original wording.

detail.before: Matthias bookmarked pages in Raindrop.io, and the page itself stayed out on the web where it could change.
detail.after: Linkwarden saves each page with a screenshot and a PDF on the Core, so he can reread it as it was.
steps: Open the page before it changes
Save it in Linkwarden
Open the saved copy later
detail.fact: Linkwarden saves web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Six pages out of eighty
popup.body: A long council report arrives as one PDF. Matthias splits out the six pages he needs in Stirling-PDF on the Core and leaves the rest.

detail.before: Pulling pages from a big PDF meant uploading the whole report to Smallpdf, including pages he had no need to send.
detail.after: Stirling-PDF splits the report on the Core. Matthias saves just the pages he needs as their own file.
steps: Open the report in Stirling-PDF
Pick the pages he needs
Save them as a new file
detail.fact: Stirling-PDF merges, splits, compresses and converts PDFs on your own Core.

beats.capability: edit audio in a browser tab: cut, fade, normalise and export

popup.title: One quote cut from the tape
popup.body: Matthias listens through headphones and marks one quote. AudioMass cuts it from a copy on the Core, so the whole tape stays as it was.

detail.before: Matthias cut clips in TwistedWave, with the original recording and the clip kept in one project.
detail.after: AudioMass opens in a browser tab on the Core. He cuts the clip from a copy and leaves the original recording alone.
steps: Open a copy of the tape
Mark the quote and cut it
Export the clip and check it by ear
detail.fact: AudioMass edits audio in a browser tab: cut, fade, normalise and export.

beats.capability: an agent that talks to you through the messaging platform you pick, running on your Core

popup.title: Caraway drafts the chase note
popup.body: The records office is late with its reply. Matthias texts Caraway three lines, then reads the draft, changes a date and sends the note himself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: matthias
say.text: Chase note drafted. Please check the dates first.

detail.before: A late reply meant finding the thread, rereading it and writing the chase from a blank page.
detail.after: Matthias texts Caraway a few lines. Caraway drafts the chase on the Core’s local model, and Matthias reads it, fixes it and sends it himself.
steps: Text Caraway three lines
Read the draft and fix the date
Send the note himself
detail.fact: Hermes is an agent that talks to you through the messaging platform you pick, running in its own sandbox on your Core.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite in your browser, with your files on your Core

popup.title: The draft stays in one file
popup.body: Matthias writes the feature in LibreOffice in his browser, with the file on the Core. The editor gets a PDF copy by email when it is ready.

detail.before: Drafts lived in Google Workspace documents, and every version stayed with the rented suite.
detail.after: LibreOffice opens the draft in a browser tab, and the file stays on the Core. Matthias exports a PDF for his editor.
steps: Open the draft from the Core
Write and revise in the browser
Export a PDF for the editor
detail.fact: LibreOffice is an office suite you open in your browser, with your files kept on your Core.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for notes, shopping, chores and expenses, with a recipe book

popup.title: One board for the whole week
popup.body: Three people share one small kitchen and a crowded week. Dinners, the shopping list and the school dates sit in one HomeHub on the Core.

detail.before: Dinners were on a note, the shopping sat in a Cozi list and the school dates hung on the fridge.
detail.after: HomeHub keeps notes, shopping, chores and expenses in one household hub on the Core, with a recipe book.
steps: Plan the week’s dinners in the recipe book
Add what is missing to the shopping list
Pin the school dates as a note
detail.fact: HomeHub is a shared household hub for notes, shopping, chores and expenses, with a recipe book and an expiry tracker.

beats.capability: lightweight checklists and notes with Kanban boards and sharing

popup.title: Pitches move across the fridge
popup.body: Matthias moves paper cards across the fridge door as a pitch goes from idea to filed. The same columns live in Jotty on the Core.

detail.before: The pitch board lived in a Trello account, one more tab beside the paper cards on the fridge.
detail.after: Jotty keeps the same columns as a Kanban board on the Core, so the fridge cards and the board agree.
steps: Write each pitch on a card
Move the card across the fridge
Move it across the board too
detail.fact: Jotty has lightweight checklists and notes with Kanban boards and sharing.

beats.capability: design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: The poster proof on the counter
popup.body: Lindiwe lays out the winter campaign poster in Penpot on the Core. She prints a proof and props it by the kettle to check the type.

detail.before: The poster layout lived in a Figma file, and each revision was another copy in the same place.
detail.after: Penpot hosts the layout on the Core. Lindiwe revises it there and exports a proof when the type looks right.
steps: Lay out the poster in Penpot
Export a proof and print it
Fix the type and export again
detail.fact: Penpot designs and prototypes in a web-based design tool you host.

beats.capability: archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them

popup.title: The tenancy papers have one home
popup.body: The tenancy agreement, the boiler certificate and the deposit receipt used to live in three places. Now Papra archives all three on the Core.

detail.before: The tenancy papers sat in an email attachment, a Google Drive folder and a drawer.
detail.after: Papra archives the tenancy agreement, the boiler certificate and the deposit receipt on the Core, ready when the landlord asks.
steps: Scan or drop in each paper
Name each paper for what it is
Find all three in one place
detail.fact: Papra archives the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them.

beats.capability: turn a folder of photos and videos into a feed with albums and a timeline

popup.title: Tamsin’s paintings become a gallery
popup.body: Lindiwe photographs each finished painting and drops the pictures in one folder. Foldergram turns the folder into a feed with albums and a timeline.

detail.before: Tamsin’s paintings piled up on the fridge door, then in a drawer, and the best ones were hard to find.
detail.after: Foldergram turns the folder of photos into a feed on the Core, with albums and a timeline of her paintings.
steps: Photograph each finished painting
Drop the pictures in the folder
Scroll back through the albums
detail.fact: Foldergram turns a folder of photos and videos into a feed with albums and a timeline.

beats.capability: send files between phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi

popup.title: A drawing crosses the room
popup.body: Tamsin finishes a drawing on her tablet and picks Matthias’s laptop in PairDrop. The drawing lands in his folder before she has put the pencil down.

detail.before: A drawing reached the laptop through AirDrop or a message, one picture at a time.
detail.after: PairDrop sends the drawing across the home Wi-Fi from the tablet to the laptop, with nothing sent anywhere else.
steps: Open PairDrop on the tablet and the laptop
Pick the laptop
Send the drawing
detail.fact: PairDrop sends files between phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: Thursday is painting day
popup.body: Tamsin picks Thursday for the next painting, and Matthias adds the block to Companion Planning on the Core. She ticks it off when the paint is dry.

detail.before: Painting days were promised out loud and forgotten by Thursday, with nothing written down.
detail.after: Companion Planning keeps the block in one local file on the Core, beside the rest of the week.
steps: Pick the day with Tamsin
Add the block to Companion Planning
Tick it off when the paint is dry
detail.fact: Companion Planning plans tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core.

beats.capability: plan your day, track time and run a timer

popup.title: Monday’s three jobs, in order
popup.body: Monday starts with three campaign jobs on a scrap of paper. Lindiwe types them into Super Productivity on the Core and starts the timer on the first.

detail.before: The day’s tasks lived in Asana, with the campaign jobs mixed in among everyone else’s.
detail.after: Super Productivity keeps the day’s plan and its timer on the Core, one task for each campaign job.
steps: Write the three jobs as tasks
Put them in the order of the day
Start the timer on the first
detail.fact: Super Productivity plans your day, tracks time and runs a Pomodoro timer.

beats.capability: write and send newsletters to your own mailing list

popup.title: The supporter list comes home
popup.body: Lindiwe brings the charity’s supporter list in from the old mailing tool. Listmonk on the Core now holds the list and the draft of Thursday’s newsletter.
popup.note: Sending at volume needs an outside mail provider.

detail.before: The supporter list and its drafts lived in Mailchimp, and every newsletter was built there.
detail.after: Listmonk keeps the list and the drafts on the Core. Lindiwe writes the newsletter there and picks the mail provider that sends it.
steps: Import the supporter list
Write Thursday’s newsletter
Choose how it is sent
detail.fact: Listmonk writes and sends newsletters to your own mailing list.

beats.capability: resize and compress images in the browser

popup.title: Photos sized for the leaflet
popup.body: Lindiwe drops the drive’s photos into Mazanoke on the Core and picks a smaller size for the leaflet. The photos are resized in her browser tab, with no upload.

detail.before: Photos for the leaflet went through an online resizer, one picture at a time.
detail.after: Mazanoke resizes a batch of photos in the browser tab and saves the small copies beside the originals on the Core.
steps: Drop the photos into Mazanoke
Pick the size for the leaflet
Save the small copies beside the originals
detail.fact: Mazanoke resizes and compresses images in the browser, with no upload.

beats.capability: a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy

popup.title: Rooibos fills the drive tracker
popup.body: Lindiwe reads out the leaflet drops from the shelf. Rooibos opens Grist in its own browser and fills the tracker. Lindiwe reads every row before it stands.

say.speaker: lindiwe
say.text: Tracker filled. Please read each row first.

detail.before: Each drop was typed into an Airtable base by hand, a row at a time, after the leaflets were counted.
detail.after: Rooibos opens Grist in its own browser and fills a row for each drop from Lindiwe’s list. Lindiwe reads every row before it stands.
steps: Read out the week’s leaflet drops
Rooibos fills a row for each one
Read every row before it stands
detail.fact: Grist is a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy.

beats.capability: capture quick notes and journal entries in Markdown

popup.title: Next steps, jotted outdoors
popup.body: After a call on the court bench, Lindiwe jots the next steps into Memos on her phone. The note is on the Core when she is at her desk.

detail.before: The next steps after a partner’s call were typed into a Google Keep note, lost among all the others.
detail.after: Memos keeps the note as Markdown on the Core, so the next steps are in a file she can search.
steps: Jot the next steps right after the call
Add the partner’s name as a tag
Search the notes before the next call
detail.fact: Memos captures quick notes and journal entries in Markdown.

beats.capability: save articles to read later without a hosted bookmarking service

popup.title: Sunday’s long reads wait outside
popup.body: Matthias keeps the week’s long reads for Sunday morning on the court bench. Readeck holds each saved article on the Core, ready on a phone in the sun.

detail.before: Matthias saved long reads to Instapaper through the week and opened them all at once on Sunday.
detail.after: Readeck keeps the saved articles on the Core, and Matthias opens them on his phone out in the court.
steps: Save an article through the week
Open Readeck on the phone on Sunday
Read it out on the bench
detail.fact: Readeck saves articles to read later without a hosted bookmarking service.

popup.title: One Core up the stairs
popup.body: From the alcove to the back court, one Companion Core serves the flat, and the easel is still wet.

closing.body: Lindiwe’s lists, Matthias’s notes and Tamsin’s paintings sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and choose your first apps.

notes: Told in the v3 shape: nineteen of twenty-two room beats are pairs. The three pair-less beats are the Hermes chase note, Foldergram and Companion Planning; none of them replaces anything in the catalog.
The plan lists Pi-hole for the network: the flat has no camera of the family’s own, so Frigate is not told. Paperless-ngx is over the fleet app cap (Papra holds the tenancy papers).
Tamsin is six: no chat model and no agent in her beats (age rule 16). The maker pool has no app a child uses, so her pool beat is Companion Planning, a block Matthias adds for the day she picks.

LinkStack is a limit card: the page is tested over the home Wi-Fi and the note says only devices there reach it. Listmonk carries the mail provider note and promises no delivery. No beat anchors on a bed.

The Front Balcony is 1 m deep and the camera cannot stand in it, so the garden chapter is the back court bench (patio-seat). It sits last before the outro: two cuts in all, the walk out and the walk round to the street.
No third-party app is in more than two of the six apartments: Mazanoke (pair-less) and Memos replace Inkscape and Twenty, which are told in two other flats.
